ekaṅgikadvaṅgikativaṅgikāni.meaning_2: having one factor, two factors and three factors; single-factored, two-factored and three-factored
ekaṅgikadvaṅgikativaṅgikāni.construction: eka + aṅgika + dvi + aṅgika + ti + aṅgika
ekaṅgikadvaṅgikativaṅgikāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound qualifying the classes of offences (āpatti) classified by one, two or three factors of arising; neuter plural ending -āni in the text.
ekaṅgikadvaṅgikativaṅgikāni.example_1: Samuṭṭhānavidhinti sabbāpattīnaṃ kāyo vācā kāyavācā kāyacittaṃ vācācittaṃ kāyavācācittanti imāni ekaṅgikadvaṅgikativaṅgikāni.
ekaṅgikadvaṅgikativaṅgikāni.translation_1: “Method of arising” (samuṭṭhānavidhi) refers to these—single-factored, two-factored, and three-factored—in relation to all offenses: body, speech, body-speech, body-mind, speech-mind, and body-speech-mind.

saṃmuñjaniyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular in the text (saṃmuñjaniyā), listed with the winnowing basket (suppa) as a household broom. Sometimes spelt sammuñjanī. Rare; the exact formation is uncertain (possibly from √uñch, glean, sweep).
saṃmuñjaniyā.example_1: Yaṃ pana dvāre ṭhito mātugāmo bhājanadhovanaudakaṃ chaḍḍeti, tassa patanaṭṭhānañca mātugāmeneva antogehe ṭhitena pakatiyā bahi khittassa suppassa vā saṃmuñjaniyā vā patanaṭṭhānañca gharassa purato dvīsu koṇesu sambandhitvā majjhe rukkhasūcidvāraṃ ṭhapetvā gorūpānaṃ pavesananivāraṇatthaṃ kataparikkhepo ca ayaṃ sabbopi gharūpacāro nāma.
saṃmuñjaniyā.translation_1: The “house-periphery” is the space where a woman standing at the door throws out water for washing dishes, or the space where something thrown from inside the house naturally falls—like the space where a winnowing basket or a broom naturally drops something—or the area in front of a house, including the two front corners, connected to a gate of wooden bars set up to prevent cattle from entering.

saṃvidhāvahāro.meaning_2: theft by prior arrangement; conspiring together to steal; planned conspiracy to steal
saṃvidhāvahāro.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A kind of theft (avahāra) classified in the Vinaya and commentarial literature. Formed from the absolutive saṃvidhāya with loss of the initial a of avahāra (ya-lopa). The text explains it as stealing after agreeing together and consulting. Nominative singular in the sentence.
saṃvidhāvahāro.translation_1: Prior theft, theft with a method, combined theft, arranged-signal theft, and sign-theft.
saṃvidhāvahāro.example_2: Saṃvidhāvahāro nāma ‘‘ asukaṃ nāma bhaṇḍaṃ avaharissāmā ’’ ti saṃvidahitvā saṃmantayitvā avaharaṇaṃ.
saṃvidhāvahāro.translation_2: Combined theft is stealing by agreeing together and consulting to steal such-and-such property.

saṃmantayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of the causative saṃmanteti (√mant + *e). Used with saṃvidahitvā to describe thieves plotting together. The PEU analysis manta + ṇaya + tvā points to the same causative formation.
saṃmantayitvā.example_1: Saṃvidhāvahāro nāma ‘‘ asukaṃ nāma bhaṇḍaṃ avaharissāmā ’’ ti saṃvidahitvā saṃmantayitvā avaharaṇaṃ.
saṃmantayitvā.translation_1: Combined theft is stealing by agreeing together and consulting to steal such-and-such property.

chaṭṭetvā.meaning_2: having thrown away; having abandoned; having discarded
chaṭṭetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā; in the text it means 'having thrown away' (the stolen goods), with a double -ṭṭ- for chaḍḍetvā. Same meaning as chaḍḍetvā, used in the commentary.
chaṭṭetvā.example_1: ‘‘ Coro coro ’’ ti anubandho chaṭṭetvā palāyati, rakkhati.
chaṭṭetvā.translation_1: If he is followed by [cries of] 'Thief! Thief!' and throws it away and flees, he is safe.

saṃcetetvā.meaning_2: having made think; having caused to reflect; having urged on
saṃcetetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it glosses sañcicca as saṃcetetvā saddhiṃ cetetvā, i.e. 'having thought together, having considered'. Causative absolutive of saṃceteti; cf. √cit 1 (gather, accumulate) and the gloss cetetvā.
saṃcetetvā.translation_1: Regarding the third [Pārājika], the word intentionally (sañcicca) means having reflected, having pondered together.

ususattiyantapāsāṇādīnaṃ.meaning_2: arrows, spears, traps, stones and so on; such things as bows and arrows, weapons, traps and rocks
ususattiyantapāsāṇādīnaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive plural in the text, depending on nissajjanaṃ. A dvandva-style compound ending in -ādi ('and so on').
ususattiyantapāsāṇādīnaṃ.example_1: Nissaggiyoti dūre ṭhitaṃ māretukāmassa kāyena vā kāyappaṭibaddhena vā ususattiyantapāsāṇādīnaṃ nissajjanaṃ.
ususattiyantapāsāṇādīnaṃ.translation_1: Relinquished (nissaggiyo) means the casting of arrows, spears, traps, stones, etc., by one who desires to kill someone standing far away, using the body or a body-connected object.

vijjāparijappanaṃ.meaning_2: muttering of spells; recitation of incantations (for a purpose)
vijjāparijappanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The comment appears to explain vijjāmayo as involving the recitation of spells (vijjā) for the purpose of killing. The second element is uncertain; possibly parijappana (murmuring) rather than pariyāpanna. Accusative singular in the text.
vijjāparijappanaṃ.translation_1: Magic-based (vijjāmayo) means the muttering of spells for the purpose of killing.

nīlādivaṇṇasuttakusumakahāpaṇamālāsuvaṇṇ.meaning_2: in blue and so on coloured thread, flowers, coins, garlands, gold ribbons, strings of pearls, etc.
nīlādivaṇṇasuttakusumakahāpaṇamālāsuvaṇṇ.construction: nīla + ādi + vaṇṇa + sutta + kusuma + kahāpaṇa + mālā + suvaṇṇa + cīraka + muttā + vaḷi + ādi
nīlādivaṇṇasuttakusumakahāpaṇamālāsuvaṇṇ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Long bahubba-hī compound in the Veṇī explanation; locative plural agree-ing with aññataramissehi. cīraka here 'gold ribbon' rather than 'bark garment'.
nīlādivaṇṇasuttakusumakahāpaṇamālāsuvaṇṇ.example_1: Veṇī nāma vinandhitvā vā avinandhitvā vā suddhakesehi vā nīlādivaṇṇasuttakusumakahāpaṇamālāsuvaṇṇacīrakamuttāvaḷiādīsu aññataramissehi vā katakesakalāpassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ.
nīlādivaṇṇasuttakusumakahāpaṇamālāsuvaṇṇ.translation_1: Hair-braid (veṇī) is a designation for a made-up hair-knot, whether bound or unbound, whether of natural hair or mixed with blue, etc., colored thread, flowers, coins, garlands, gold ribbons, strings of pearls, etc.

saṃbhinnāsi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Part of the insulting address saṃbhinnāsi (= saṃbhinno + asi) in the saṅghādisesa passage; nominative singular in the text.
saṃbhinnāsi.example_1: Saṅghādisesoti dvinnaṃ maggānaṃ vasena vaṇṇāvaṇṇehi vā methunayācanādīhi vā ‘‘ sikharaṇīsi, saṃbhinnāsi, ubhatobyañjanakāsī ’’ ti imesu tīsu aññatarena akkosavacanena vā mātugāmaṃ obhāsantassa saṅghādiseso nāma āpattinikāyo hotīti.
saṃbhinnāsi.translation_1: Entailing a formal meeting of the Order (saṅghādiseso) means that for a monk who addresses a woman by way of the two tracts, or by way of praise or blame, or by way of requesting sexual intercourse, etc., or by way of one of the three insulting words—‘you are deformed,’ ‘you are penetrated,’ ‘you are hermaphrodite’—there is a class of offense called saṅghādisesa.

saṃcaraṇabhāvaṃ.meaning_2: state of moving between; acting as a go-between
saṃcaraṇabhāvaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, glossing sañcarittaṃ. The first member is a noun of the gerund-like in -aṇa formation (compare sañcaraṇa > saṃcaraṇa before the voiced consonant), not a separate root derivation.
saṃcaraṇabhāvaṃ.translation_1: In the fifth, “acting as a go-between” means the state of moving back and forth between a man and a woman.

āvijjhituṃ.meaning_2: to turn around; to go around
āvijjhituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive from āvijjhati, meaning to turn a cart around. The text describes turning a cart by placing one wheel outside the eaves-drip. Alternate spelling āvijjituṃ.
āvijjhituṃ.example_1: Tehi bhikkhūhi vatthu desetabbaṃ anārambhaṃ saparikkamananti tehi bhikkhūhi kipillikādīnaṃ āsayādīhi terasahi, pubbaṇṇāparaṇṇanissitādīhi soḷasahi upaddavehi virahitattā anārambhaṃ, dvīhi vā catūhi vā balibaddhehi yuttena sakaṭena ekaṃ cakkaṃ nibbodakapatanaṭṭhāne ekaṃ bahi katvā āvijjhituṃ sakkuṇeyyatāya saparikkamananti sallakkhetvā sace saṅghapahonakā honti, tattheva, no ce, saṅghamajjhaṃ gantvā tena bhikkhunā yācitehi ñattidutiyena kammena vatthu desetabbaṃ.
āvijjhituṃ.translation_1: “Those monks should approve a site where no harm will be done and which has an open space around it” means those monks, having noted that it is free from the sixteen dangers starting with the nests of ants, etc., and the sixteen dangers including those dwelling on crops and pulses—and thus harm-free—and that it has an open space because it is possible to turn around [a cart] with two or four oxen by placing one wheel outside the eaves-drip—and thus it has an open space—if they are enough, they should approve the site right there; if not, having gone to the midst of the Sangha, the site should be approved for him by the Sangha through a formal act with two announcements.

paṭipātiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular of paṭipāti, used adverbially in the sense 'in order, one after another'. Sometimes spelled paṭipāṭiyā.
paṭipātiyā.example_1: Sāmīcippaṭikkhepo nāma abhivādanapaccuṭṭhānaañjalikammasāmīcikammabījanikammādīnaṃ akaraṇaṃ, taṃ paṭipātiyā vandanādīni karoto ekassa akatvā sesānaṃ karaṇakāle veditabbaṃ.
paṭipātiyā.translation_1: Rejecting appropriate conduct (sāmīcippaṭikkhepo) means not performing actions such as salutation, rising in greeting, hand-folding, respectful behavior, and fanning; this should be understood when one who is performing salutations and so on performs them for all except one [monk].

upaparikkhiyamāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle masculine nominative singular, commenting on anuvijjiyamāno. Not a finite verb form.
upaparikkhiyamāno.example_1: Samanuggāhīyamāno vāti anuvijjakena kiṃ te diṭṭhantiādinā nayena anuvijjiyamāno upaparikkhiyamāno.
upaparikkhiyamāno.translation_1: Samanuggāhīyamāno vā means: being investigated or examined by an inquirer [asking] by way of [questions] like 'What have you seen?', etc.

anodisakaṃ.meaning_2: not specified; not particularised; not pointed out
anodisakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text accusative singular modifying dhammaṃ: dhamma not specified to a particular person. A negative compound with the prefix na (an-).
anodisakaṃ.example_1: Vuṭṭhānādhippāyena ‘‘ tvaṃ itthannāmaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno, taṃ paṭikarohī ’’ ti vadantassa, uposathaṃ vā pavāraṇaṃ vā ṭhapentassa ca okāsakammaṃ natthi, ṭhapanakkhettaṃ pana jānitabbaṃ, anuvijjakassāpi osaṭe vatthusmiṃ ‘‘ atthetaṃ tavā ’’ ti anuvijjanādhippāyena vadantassa okāsakammaṃ natthi, dhammakathikassāpi ‘‘ yo idañca idañca karoti, ayaṃ assamaṇo ’’ tiādinā nayena anodisakaṃ dhammaṃ kathentassa okāsakammaṃ natthi.
anodisakaṃ.translation_1: For one saying, 'You have fallen into such-and-such an offense; confess it,' out of an intention for rehabilitation, or for one delaying Uposatha or Pavāraṇā, there is no need for a formal act of request; however, the time for the delay should be known; also for a vinaya-expert [who is asked] when the matter has arisen [in the assembly]—if he speaks out of an intention to investigate, saying, 'Is this yours?', there is no need for a formal act of request; [and] for a preacher of Dhamma who speaks out of an intention to investigate, saying [something] by way of 'Whoever does this and that, this person is not a monk,' there is no need for a formal act of request.

māiti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text māiti is mā + iti; the quotation is analysed as mā parakkami, mā aṭṭhāsī 'do not strive, do not stand still'. Prohibitive particle used with aorist/imperative.
māiti.example_1: Ettha ca māiti padaṃ ‘‘ parakkamī ’’ tipadena ‘‘ aṭṭhāsī ’’ tipadena ca saddhiṃ ‘‘ mā parakkami, mā aṭṭhāsī ’’ ti yojetabbaṃ.
māiti.translation_1: And here, the term 'Venerable sir' should be applied with the term 'strive' and the term 'persist'.

sotiādimhi.meaning_2: in the soti and so on; in sotiādi
sotiādimhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular of sotiādi, the first of a list beginning with soti; see soti sotaṃ. Sandhi of ādimhi with the final i of soti.

odhānasamodhāno.meaning_2: composite by shaking off (a Vinaya probation); combining by deduction; name of a kind of probation (parivāsa)
odhānasamodhāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vinaya technical term for the parivāsa calculated by shaking off (odhunitvā) the days already undergone and adding (samodahitvā) the later offence to the earlier one. Nominative singular in the text, parallel to agghasamodhāna and missakasamodhāna.
odhānasamodhāno.example_1: Itaro pana samodhānaparivāso nāma, so tividho hoti odhānasamodhāno agghasamodhāno missakasamodhānoti.
odhānasamodhāno.translation_1: The other one is called 'composite-probation', and it is threefold: odhāna-composite, aggha-composite, and missaka-composite.
odhānasamodhāno.example_2: Tattha odhānasamodhāno nāma antarāpattiṃ āpajjitvā paṭicchādentassa parivutthadivase odhunitvā makkhetvā purimāya āpattiyā mūladivasaparicchede pacchā āpannaṃ āpattiṃ samodahitvā dātabbaparivāso vuccati.
odhānasamodhāno.translation_2: Among these, odhāna-composite is called the probation given by shaking off the days of probation already undergone for an intermediate offense incurred while concealing, and by adding the later incurred offense to the original offense in terms of the initial day's duration.

abhietabbo.meaning_2: to be brought in; to be rehabilitated; to be accepted
abhietabbo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant spelling of abbhetabba (abbhetabbo in the text). Used in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī to gloss abbhetabbo as abhietabbo, sampaṭicchitabbo. Potential participle in -tabba from abhi + √i, with the causative sense 'to be brought in' (abbhānakamma).
abhietabbo.example_1: Abbhetabboti abhietabbo, sampaṭicchitabbo, abbhānakammavasena osāretabboti vuttaṃ hoti.
abhietabbo.translation_1: 'To be rehabilitated' means should be accepted, should be admitted into the Sangha by way of the rehabilitation act—this is what is said.

akatabbhānakammoti.meaning_2: whose rehabilitation ceremony has not been performed; not having undergone the abbhāna rite
akatabbhānakammoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Predicative compound describing a bhikkhu; the cited form has -ti (iti) attached: akatabbhānakammoti.
akatabbhānakammoti.example_1: Anabbhitoti na abbhito asampaṭicchito, akatabbhānakammoti vuttaṃ hoti.
akatabbhānakammoti.translation_1: 'Not rehabilitated' means not accepted, one who has not had the rehabilitation act performed—this is what is said.

paṭidentassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive singular in the text (na paṭidentassa, 'of one who does not return'). The PEU gives the split Pati+dā+a+anta; the form is built on the present stem paṭidena-.
paṭidentassa.example_1: Nissaṭṭhavatthuṃ ‘‘ dinnamidaṃ iminā mayhan ’’ ti saññāya na paṭidentassa dukkaṭaṃ, tassa santakabhāvaṃ ñatvā lesena acchindanto sāmikassa dhuranikkhepena bhaṇḍaṃ agghāpetvā kāretabboti.
paṭidentassa.translation_1: An offense of wrong conduct (dukkaṭaṃ) is incurred by one who does not return a relinquished item, thinking 'This was given to me by so-and-so' with the perception that it is their own property. Knowing it belongs to the owner, one who seizes it through a ruse should be dealt with by the owner having determined its value and having relinquished the burden.

rajāpanākoṭāpanesupi.meaning_2: causing to be dyed and causing to be beaten
rajāpanākoṭāpanesupi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative plural in the text, in the phrase rajāpanākoṭāpanesupi, meaning that the same rule applies also to getting a robe dyed or beaten. The ending -esu has assimilated to the following -pi.
rajāpanākoṭāpanesupi.example_1: Dhovāpeyya vāti sace ‘‘ dhovā ’’ tivācāya vadati, kāyavikāraṃ vā karoti, hatthena vā hatthe deti, pādamūle vā ṭhapeti, antodvādasahatthe okāse ṭhatvā upari vā khipati, aññassa vā hatthe peseti, tāya dhotaṃ, dhovāpitameva hoti, rajāpanākoṭāpanesupi eseva nayo.
rajāpanākoṭāpanesupi.translation_1: 'Have it washed' means if one says by word, 'Wash [this]', or makes a bodily gesture, or gives it into the hand, or places it at the feet, or standing within a twelve-cubit space, throws it above, or sends it by another's hand—it is considered washed or had washed; the same method applies to having it dyed or beaten.
rajāpanākoṭāpanesupi.example_2: Upāsakassa vā sāmaṇerassa vā hatthe dinnaṃ hoti, so ce liṅge parivatte upasampajjitvā dhovati, daharassa bhikkhussa vā dinnaṃ hoti, sopi liṅge parivatte dhovati, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyameva, rajāpanākoṭāpanesupi eseva nayo.
rajāpanākoṭāpanesupi.translation_2: If it is given into the hand of a male lay follower or a novice, and he, upon changing his status, receives higher ordination and washes it, or if it is given to a young monk, and he, upon changing his status, washes it, it is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession; the same method applies to dyeing or beating.

harīṭakakkhaṇḍampi.meaning_2: piece of myrobalan fruit; bit of a myrobalan
harīṭakakkhaṇḍampi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text harīṭakakkhaṇḍampi is harīṭakakkhaṇḍaṃ + api, with the consonant doubled before -pi; the meaning is 'even a piece of myrobalan', used as an example of something trivial. The word is accusative singular.
harīṭakakkhaṇḍampi.example_1: Aññatra pārivattakāti yaṃ ‘‘ antamaso harīṭakakkhaṇḍampi datvā vā dassāmī ’’ ti ābhogaṃ katvā vā pārivattakaṃ gaṇhāti, taṃ ṭhapetvā aññaṃ antamaso vikappanupagaṃ paṭaparissāvanampi gaṇhantassa nissaggiyaṃ hoti.
harīṭakakkhaṇḍampi.translation_1: 'Except in exchange' means that having made a mental effort—even if it is just [by promising] to give back a piece of myrobalan—if one takes that in exchange, excluding that, if one accepts anything else, even a [simple] cloth filter, it is subject to relinquishment.

vatātiādimāha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of vata, iti, ādiṃ and āha; quotation with iti. The final word āha is the perfect of √ah (say), but is treated as part of the sandhi compound.

vātiidaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of vāti (ind, 'or', formed from vā + iti) with idaṃ. No sentences supplied, so the analysis is based on the form alone.

dvādasakkhattuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] dvādasa + khattuṃ (times) with doubling of the initial consonant; an adverb of number.
dvādasakkhattuṃ.example_1: Tattha yo ekadivasameva punappunaṃ gantvā chakkhattuṃ codeti, sakiṃyeva vā gantvā ‘‘ attho me, āvuso, cīvarenā ’’ ti chakkhattuṃ vadati, tathā ekadivasameva punappunaṃ gantvā dvādasakkhattuṃ tiṭṭhati, sakiṃyeva vā gantvā tatra tatra ṭhāne tiṭṭhati, sopi sabbacodanāyo sabbaṭṭhānāni ca bhañjati, ko pana vādo nānādivasesu evaṃ karontassāti ayamettha vinicchayo.
dvādasakkhattuṃ.translation_1: In that case, whoever goes and prompts six times in just one day, or goes once and speaks [of the need] six times in one day, [or] goes again and again and stands twelve times in one day, or goes once and stands in various places, he breaks all [allowed] promptings and all [allowed] standings; what then should be said of one doing so on different days? This is the decision here.

mukhavevaṭikakappiyakārako.meaning_2: one who provides services while facing the bhikkhu; face-to-face attendant
mukhavevaṭikakappiyakārako.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The word is a compound. In the Vinaya a kappiyakāraka is a layman who makes things allowable for bhikkhus. Here mukhavevaṭika means 'facing the bhikkhu' in contrast to parammukha, 'facing the donor', the one who might accept things on behalf of the bhikkhu. Nominative singular in the text.
mukhavevaṭikakappiyakārako.example_1: Yo pana ubhohi pi aniddiṭṭho mukhavevaṭikakappiyakārako ca parammukhakappiyakārako ca, so na kiñci vattabbo, evaṃ idha dasapi kappiyakārakā dassitā honti.
mukhavevaṭikakappiyakārako.translation_1: But regarding those who are not designated by either [the bhikkhu or the donor], namely the 'face-to-face attendant' and the 'non-face-to-face attendant,' one should not speak to them; ten such servants are shown here.

vippakatapaayosāpananayena.meaning_2: by the method of finishing what was begun by oneself
vippakatapaayosāpananayena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular used adverbially. The reading 'paayosāpana' looks like a scribal error for 'payosāpana' (payosāpana, finishing, completing). Probably a compound, but not a standard formation; treat as an indeclinable phrase in this text.
vippakatapaayosāpananayena.example_1: Āḷaviyaṃ chabbaggiye ārabbha kosiyamissakaṃ santhataṃ kārāpanavatthusmiṃ paññattaṃ, asādhāraṇapaññatti, attano atthāya kārāpanavasena sāṇattikaṃ, attanā vippakatapaayosāpananayena catukkapācittiyaṃ, aññassatthāya karaṇakārāpanesu aññena kataṃ paṭilabhitvā paribhuñjane ca dukkaṭaṃ.
vippakatapaayosāpananayena.translation_1: It was prescribed at Āḷavī regarding the group of six bhikkhus in the context of having a rug mixed with silk made; it is an uncommon laying down, a triple offense of expiation due to having it made for one's own benefit, a fourfold offense of expiation by the method of finishing what was begun by oneself, and an offense of wrong conduct in [the effort of] having it made for someone else's benefit, or in using it after having received it [already] made by another.

anuttaṇḍulamakilinnamapiṇḍikaṃ.meaning_2: free of unbroken rice; without husk-free grains; with no (grains that are) not rice
anuttaṇḍulamakilinnamapiṇḍikaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the compound anuttaṇḍulamakilinnamapiṇḍikaṃ, describing cooked rice free of raw grains, uncooked lumps and stickiness; accusative singular agreeing with odanaṃ.
anuttaṇḍulamakilinnamapiṇḍikaṃ.example_1: Tatrāyaṃ vinicchayo – anupahatapurāṇasālitaṇḍulānaṃ sukoṭṭitaparisuddhānaṃ dve magadhanāḷiyo gahetvā tehi taṇḍulehi anuttaṇḍulamakilinnamapiṇḍikaṃ suvisadaṃ kundamakuḷarāsisadisaṃ avassāvitodanaṃ pacitvā niravasesaṃ patte pakkhipitvā tassa odanassa catutthabhāgappamāṇo nātighano nātitanuko hatthahāriyo sabbasambhārasaṅkhato muggasūpo pakkhipitabbo, tato ālopassa anurūpaṃ yāvacarimālopappahonakaṃ macchamaṃsādibyañjanaṃ pakkhipitabbaṃ, sappitelatakkarasakañjiyādīni pana gaṇanūpagāni na honti.
anuttaṇḍulamakilinnamapiṇḍikaṃ.translation_1: The determination here is: having taken two Magadha-measures of uncrushed old fine rice, cleaned and well-pounded, having cooked them to be neither undercooked, soggy, nor clumpy, but very clean, like a cluster of jasmine buds, and drained, one should place it all into the bowl; into that, one should put a portion of bean soup—a quarter-measure of that rice, not too thick or too thin, able to be carried by hand, and prepared with all necessary ingredients; following that, one should put fish, meat, or other side-dishes corresponding to each mouthful, sufficient for the last mouthful; but items such as ghee, oil, and fermented liquids are not counted.

paṭisāyitabbāni.meaning_2: should be enjoyed; should be consumed; to be partaken of
paṭisāyitabbāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Neuter plural nominative in the text, glossed by the commentary as paṭisāyitabbāni = paribhuñjitabbāni; the variant reading paṭisāyanīyāni is the same formation with the -anīya suffix.
paṭisāyitabbāni.translation_1: In the third, 'which are to be acknowledged' means: they are to be enjoyed; they should be used, is the meaning.

metiādivacanena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Unrecognised and possibly corrupt form with no sentence context; cannot be analysed reliably. Likely a quotation or scribal error. Instrumental singular ending -ena suggests a noun in -a, perhaps containing mettā ('loving-kindness').

paridahitabbā.meaning_2: to be worn; should be worn
paridahitabbā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Potential participle of paridahati, used in the sense of a duty (should be worn). Feminine nominative singular in the text, agreeing with the robe implicit from the context.
paridahitabbā.example_1: Katvā nivāsetabbanti gimhānaṃ pacchimaddhamāsassa paṭhamadivasato paṭṭhāya yāva kattikamāsassa pacchimadivaso, tāva sūcikammaniṭṭhānena sakimpi vaṇṇabhedamattarajanena kappabindukaraṇena ca katvā paridahitabbā.
paridahitabbā.translation_1: “Having had it made, he should wear it” means that from the first day of the last half-month of summer until the last day of the Kattika month, he should have it finished by sewing, dye it at least once to change its color, and mark it with a cloth-mark before wearing it.

ukkaḍḍhiyati.meaning_2: is delayed; is postponed; is made to increase; is intercalated
ukkaḍḍhiyati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive/causative form of ukkaḍḍhati; in the commentary it refers to the rainy season or an intercalary month being delayed.
ukkaḍḍhiyati.example_1: Sace tasmiṃ māse atikkante vassaṃ ukkaḍḍhiyati, puna māsaparihāraṃ labhati, dhovitvā pana nikkhipitvā vassūpanāyikadivase adhiṭṭhātabbā.
ukkaḍḍhiyati.translation_1: If, after that month has passed, the rainy season is delayed or there is a leap month, he gets the privilege of an extra month; but he must wash it, put it aside, and formally establish it on the day of entering the rainy season.

ovijjhanavacane.meaning_2: piercing speech; stinging words; harsh insulting speech
ovijjhanavacane.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text, glossing omasavāda. Ovijjhana is a verbal noun from the root √vij (to pierce, shake), used here in the sense of words that pierce the ears and heart.
ovijjhanavacane.example_1: Dutiye omasavādeti ovijjhanavacane, jātināmagottakammasippaābādhaliṅgakilesaāpattiakkosesu bhūtena vā abhūtena vā yena kenaci pārājikaṃ āpannaṃ vā anāpannaṃ vā yaṃkiñci bhikkhuṃ yāya kāyaci vācāya vā hatthamuddāya vā anaññāpadesena akkosanavacane pācittiyanti attho.
ovijjhanavacane.translation_1: In the second, “insulting speech” means in a piercing, stinging manner, by way of birth, name, clan, occupation, craft, illness, appearance, defilement, offense, or insults, whether true or false, with any of the ten insulting factors, whether the bhikkhu has incurred a pārājika or has not, [when] insulting any bhikkhu with any kind of speech or hand gesture, directly, not by pointing to another, [that] is an offense of expiation.

osāpanañcāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text joined with -ca as the second factor of an offence; nominative singular in the phrase ekato osāpanañ ca. Possibly "reciting together"; cf. osāpeti.
osāpanañcāti.example_1: Anupasampannatā, vuttalakkhaṇaṃ dhammaṃ padaso vācanatā, ekato osāpanañcāti imānettha tīṇi aṅgāni.
osāpanañcāti.translation_1: The state of being not fully ordained, the act of instructing the Dhamma as described line-by-line, and the act of reciting together—these are the three factors here.

upaddhacchannaparicchannādīsu.meaning_2: beginning with a half-enclosed and partly-enclosed (dwelling); etc. half-covered and enclosed
upaddhacchannaparicchannādīsu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative plural in the text, matching the preceding 'upasampanne ... vematikassa vā' list of dwelling types; the adjective is bahubbīhi modifying a dwelling (senāsana).
upaddhacchannaparicchannādīsu.example_1: Āḷaviyaṃ sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha anupasampannena sahaseyyavatthusmiṃ paññattaṃ,‘‘ uttaridirattatirattan ’’ ti ayamettha anupaññatti, sādhāraṇapaññatti, anāṇattikaṃ, tikapācittiyaṃ, upasampanne anupasampannasaññino vematikassa vā upaddhacchannaparicchannādīsu ca dukkaṭaṃ.
upaddhacchannaparicchannādīsu.translation_1: Prescribed at Āḷavī regarding the group-of-six monks in the context of the sleeping place rule; 'beyond two or three nights' is a supplementary regulation here. It is a common laying down, it does not involve a command, there is a threefold offense of expiation. For one who is fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong conduct if he is in doubt [about whether the listener is] fully ordained or not, [and so on] for partially-enclosed [dwellings].

vikopāpeti.meaning_2: causes to be destroyed; has destroyed; gets broken up
vikopāpeti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of vikopeti; used for causing another to dig or destroy. Third person singular present in the text.
vikopāpeti.example_1: Yo pana khaṇāpeti, vuttanayeneva vikopāpeti, tassa ‘‘ imaṃ padesan ’’ ti vā ‘‘ imaṃ pathavin ’’ ti vā evaṃ niyametvā ‘‘ khaṇa, bhindā ’’ tiādinā nayena āṇāpentassa āṇattiyā dukkaṭaṃ, sakiṃ āṇatte divasampi khaṇante āṇāpakassa ekameva pācittiyaṃ, sace itaro punappunaṃ āṇāpeti, vācāya vācāya pācittiyaṃ.
vikopāpeti.translation_1: However, if one has it dug, disrupts it [as before], for one commanding, 'Dig this place,' or 'Dig this earth,' by way of such instructions, there is an offense of wrong conduct for the commander. If one who is commanded digs for the whole day [due to] one command, there is only one offense of expiation for the commander; if the other digs repeatedly, [there is] an offense of expiation for every sentence [of command].
vikopāpeti.example_2: Tasmā yo bhikkhu pathaviudakapākārādīsu yatthakatthaci jātaṃ asukkhaṃ antamaso atisukhumatiṇampi sāsapabījakasevālampi uddharaṇacchedanavijjhanādīhi vikopeti vā pathavikhaṇane vuttanayena vikopāpeti vā pācittiyaṃ āpajjati.
vikopāpeti.translation_2: Therefore, if any bhikkhu destroys—or causes to be destroyed in the manner stated for digging the earth—living, non-withered [vegetation] anywhere, such as in earth, water, walls, and so on, even down to a very delicate blade of grass, a mustard-seed-sized moss, or a small [aquatic] plant, by extracting, cutting, piercing, and so on, he commits an offense of expiation.

vikopāpanaṃ.meaning_2: causing to be damaged; causing destruction; causing harm
vikopāpanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative action noun from vikopeti (caus. of vikopayati/vikupati). In the text it is nominative singular in the phrase vikopanaṃ vā vikopāpanaṃ vā, the third of three factors. Alternative analysis: bisa form of vikopāpana.
vikopāpanaṃ.example_1: Bhūtagāmo, bhūtagāmasaññitā, vikopanaṃ vā vikopāpanaṃ vāti imānettha tīṇi aṅgāni.
vikopāpanaṃ.translation_1: The plant, the perception of it as a plant, and [either] damaging [it] or causing it to be damaged—these are the three factors here.

paṭicaraṇavatthusmiṃ.meaning_2: case of covering up; matter of evasive conduct
paṭicaraṇavatthusmiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text. In Vinaya usage vatthu means "case; matter"; the compound refers to the Channa rule on covering up one offence with another.
paṭicaraṇavatthusmiṃ.example_1: Kosambiyaṃ channattheraṃ ārabbha aññenaññaṃ paṭicaraṇavatthusmiṃ paññattaṃ, sādhāraṇapaññatti, anāṇattikaṃ, dhammakamme tikapācittiyaṃ, adhammakamme tikadukkaṭaṃ, anāropite pana aññavādake vā vihesake vā tathā karontassa dukkaṭameva.
paṭicaraṇavatthusmiṃ.translation_1: Prescribed at Kosambī regarding the elder Channa in the context of the matter of covering up one thing with another; it is a common laying down, it does not involve a command. In a lawful act, there is a threefold offense of expiation; in an unlawful act, there is a threefold offense of wrong conduct. However, for one who does so [before] the act has been imposed on an evasive speaker or a vexer, there is only an offense of wrong conduct.

paṭicaraṇaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the passage it is part of the phrase aññenaññaṃ paṭicaraṇaṃ, 'covering up one thing with another'. Nominative singular neuter. Sometimes analysed as pati + cara + yu, with the sense 'acting back against'. The PEU's 'cover/conceal' gloss agrees with the commentary's context.
paṭicaraṇaṃ.example_1: Dhammakammena āropitatā, āpattiyā vā vatthunā vā anuyuñjiyamānatā, chādetukāmatāya aññenaññaṃ paṭicaraṇaṃ vā tuṇhībhāvo vāti imānettha tīṇi aṅgāni.
paṭicaraṇaṃ.translation_1: Being imposed [by] a lawful act, being examined about an offense or a matter, and covering up one thing with another or silence [to] cover up—these three are the factors here.

saṃvellitvā.meaning_2: having wrapped up; having wound together; having bound by wrapping
saṃvellitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of saṃvellati (saṃ + √vell, to shake, sway, curl). In the sentence it describes the koccha stool being bound by winding or wrapping material together. The form is sometimes analysed as saṃ + vell + itvā.
saṃvellitvā.example_1: Kocchaṃ pana vākausīramuñjapabbajādīnaṃ aññataramayaṃ anto saṃvellitvā baddhaṃ heṭṭhā ca upari ca vitthataṃ paṇavasaṇṭhānaṃ majjhe sīhacammādiparikkhittaṃ hoti, akappiyacammaṃ nāmettha natthi.
saṃvellitvā.translation_1: A 'stool' (koccha) is made of hemp, spikenard, muñja grass, pabbaja grass, and so on, bound by wrapping in the middle, spread out at the bottom and top, with the shape of a drum, [and] surrounded in the middle with lion skin and so on; there is no unallowable skin here.

aniyyātetvā.meaning_2: not having handed over; without handing over; not having completed; without concluding
aniyyātetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Negative absolutive of niyyātetvā (causative of niyyāti/nīyati). In the first sentence it means 'without handing over (the lodging)'; in the second, 'without completing (the counsel)'.
aniyyātetvā.example_1: Anāpucchaṃ vā gaccheyyāti yo bhikkhu vā sāmaṇero vā ārāmiko vā lajjī hoti, attano palibodhaṃ viya maññati, tathārūpaṃ anāpucchitvā taṃ senāsanaṃ tassa aniyyātetvā nirapekkho gacchati, thāmamajjhimassa purisassa leḍḍupātaṃ atikkameyya, tassa ekena pādena leḍḍupātātikkame dukkaṭaṃ, dutiyapādātikkame pācittiyaṃ.
aniyyātetvā.translation_1: ‘Or go without asking for permission’ means if any conscientious bhikkhu, novice, or monastery worker considers it his own responsibility [to protect the property], and departs without asking such a person [or] without handing over that lodging to him, without regard [to the future], and exceeds the distance of a stone's throw [for] a man of average strength, [then] for the crossing of a stone's throw with the first foot [it is] an offense of wrong conduct; [for] the crossing with the second foot, [it is] an offense of expiation.
aniyyātetvā.example_2: Sace pana taṃ dhammakammaṃ hoti,‘‘ dhammakamme dhammakammasaññī samaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ samaggasaññī ovadatī ’’ ti (pāci.151) idaṃ avasānapadaṃ ṭhapetvā teneva nayena sattarasa dukkaṭāni,‘‘ samaggamhāyyā ’’ ti ca vutte aññaṃ dhammaṃ,‘‘ vaggamhāyyā ’’ ti ca vutte aṭṭha garudhamme bhaṇantassa, ovādañca aniyyātetvā aññaṃ dhammaṃ bhaṇantassa dukkaṭameva.
aniyyātetvā.translation_2: However, if that formal act is a lawful act, excluding this final statement—'one who, in a lawful act, has the perception of a lawful act, counsels a unified bhikkhunī order while having the perception of a unified order'—by that same method there are seventeen offenses of wrong conduct; and if, when told 'Venerable, we have arrived in a unified state', one recites a different Dhamma, or if, when told 'Venerable, we are divided', one recites the eight heavy Dhamma [rules], or if one recites a different Dhamma without completing the counsel, [each is] an offense of wrong conduct.

santharāpanaṃ.meaning_2: causing to be spread; having (something) spread; making (a mat, couch) laid out
santharāpanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative noun in -ana from santharati (√thar with saṃ). In the text paired with santharaṇaṃ ('spreading'), accusative singular as one of the factors (aṅga) of the dwelling place.
santharāpanaṃ.example_1: Mañcādīnaṃ saṅghikatā, vuttalakkhaṇe dese santharaṇaṃ vā santharāpanaṃ vā, apalibuddhatā, āpadāya abhāvo, nirapekkhatā, leḍḍupātātikkamoti imānettha cha aṅgāni.
santharāpanaṃ.translation_1: The Sangha-ownership of couches and so on, spreading or causing to be spread in a place with the stated characteristics, being untroubled, absence of danger, lack of disregard, and crossing the stone's throw—these six are the factors here.
santharāpanaṃ.example_2: Vuttalakkhaṇaseyyā, tassā saṅghikatā, vuttalakkhaṇe vihāre santharaṇaṃ vā santharāpanaṃ vā, apalibuddhatā, āpadāya abhāvo, anapekkhassa disāpakkamanaṃ, upacārasīmātikkamoti imānettha satta aṅgāni.
santharāpanaṃ.translation_2: The Sangha-ownership of the couch and so on, spreading or causing to be spread in a place with the stated characteristics, being untroubled, absence of danger, departure for the sake of an unconcerned [state], and crossing the stone's throw—these six are the factors here.

santharaṇasantharāpanesupi.meaning_2: spreading (a mat) and causing (it) to be spread; laying down and having laid down (bedding); (in Vinaya) spreading out and having spread out (a sleeping place)
santharaṇasantharāpanesupi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative plural in the text, governed by the same context as nisajjasayanesu. Dvanda compound; second member is a causative form (santharāpana) of √thar. Possibly read as an adjective agreeing with nisajjasayanesu.
santharaṇasantharāpanesupi.example_1: Sāvatthiyaṃ chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha anupakhajja seyyakappanavatthusmiṃ paññattaṃ, sādhāraṇapaññatti, anāṇattikaṃ, tikapācittiyaṃ, puggalike tikadukkaṭaṃ, vuttūpacārato vā bahi, upaṭṭhānasālādike vā, vihārassa upacāre vā, santharaṇasantharāpanesupi nisajjasayanesupi dukkaṭameva.
santharaṇasantharāpanesupi.translation_1: Prescribed at Sāvatthī regarding the group-of-six monks in the context of encroaching and sharing a sleeping place; it is a common laying down, it does not involve a command, there is a threefold offense of expiation, and a threefold offense of wrong conduct for property belonging to an individual. Outside the stated precinct, or in a refectory and so on, or in the precinct of the dwelling, it is only an offense of wrong conduct [for the act of] spreading or causing to be spread, and [also for] sitting or lying down.

nikkaḍḍhāpanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nom/acc singular in the text. Causative-abstract noun from nikkaḍḍhati.
nikkaḍḍhāpanaṃ.example_1: Saṅghikavihāro, upasampannassa bhaṇḍanakārakabhāvādivinimuttatā, kopena nikkaḍḍhanaṃ vā nikkaḍḍhāpanaṃ vāti imānettha tīṇi aṅgāni.
nikkaḍḍhāpanaṃ.translation_1: Sangha-ownership of the dwelling, the status of the ordained [person] as being free from [the status of] a troublemaker and so on, and evicting or causing eviction out of anger—these three are the factors here.

abhinisīdanaabhinipajjanavatthusmiṃ.meaning_2: case of sitting down and lying down (on it); matter of sitting and lying down suddenly
abhinisīdanaabhinipajjanavatthusmiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text, in a Vinaya passage about a couch with removable feet. vatthu here means 'case; matter' (not 'ground'). The first two members are action nouns from abhinisīdati and abhinipajjati.
abhinisīdanaabhinipajjanavatthusmiṃ.example_1: Sāvatthiyaṃ aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ ārabbha uparivehāsakuṭiyā āhaccapādakaṃ mañcaṃ pīṭhaṃ sahasā abhinisīdanaabhinipajjanavatthusmiṃ paññattaṃ, sādhāraṇapaññatti, anāṇattikaṃ, tikapācittiyaṃ, puggalike tikadukkaṭaṃ, attano vā, vissāsikassa vā santake vihāre, avehāsakuṭiyā, sīsaghaṭṭāya, yassa vā heṭṭhā dabbasambhārādīnaṃ nikkhittattā aparibhogaṃ hoti, uparitalaṃ vā padarasañcitaṃ sudhādiparikammakataṃ vā, tattha āhaccapādake nisīdantassa, yo ce tasmiṃ vehāsaṭṭhepi āhaccapādake ṭhito kiñci gaṇhāti vā laggati vā, yassa ca paṭāṇī dinnā hoti, pādasīsānaṃ upari āṇī pavesitā, tattha nisīdantassa, ummattakādīnañca anāpatti.
abhinisīdanaabhinipajjanavatthusmiṃ.translation_1: Prescribed at Sāvatthī regarding a certain bhikkhu in the context of sitting or lying down suddenly on a couch or chair with removable feet in a lofty cell; it is a common laying down, it does not involve a command, there is a threefold offense of expiation, and a threefold offense of wrong conduct for property belonging to an individual. [There is no offense] in one's own or an acquaintance's dwelling, [or] in a non-lofty cell, [or] when it hits the head, or when the floor below is unusable because of stored materials, or if the upper floor is planked or specially finished with plaster, [or] for one sitting on a couch or chair with removable feet therein, [or] if one stands on that couch or chair with removable feet even in that lofty location and takes or hangs anything [on a peg], or if the wedge of that [couch or chair] is already fixed and the peg is inserted above the foot-head; [there is also no offense] for the insane and so on.

limpitabbo.example_1: Tattha kiñcāpi ‘‘ idaṃ nāma kattabban ’’ ti neva mātikāyaṃ, na padabhājane vuttaṃ, aṭṭhuppattiyaṃ pana ‘‘ punappunaṃ chādāpesi, punappunaṃ lepāpesī ’’ ti (pāci.134) adhikārato yāva dvārakosā aggaḷaṭṭhapanāya punappunaṃ limpitabbo vā lepāpetabbo vāti evamattho daṭṭhabbo.
limpitabbo.translation_1: Although this procedure is not mentioned in the Summary or the Word-analysis, in the arising of the matter it is said, 'He had it thatched again and again, he had it plastered again and again.' Because of this context, the meaning should be understood as: 'one may oneself apply it or have others apply it again and again as far as the doorcase for the sake of fixing the door'.
limpitabbo.example_2: Te vivaraṇakāle vidatthimattampi atirekampi bhittippadesaṃ paharanti, upacāro panettha sabbadisāsu labbhati, tasmā sabbadisāsu kavāṭavitthārappamāṇo okāso ālokasandhiparikammatthāya limpitabbo vā lepāpetabbo vāti ayamettha adhippāyo.
limpitabbo.translation_2: When opening, they strike the wall area [at a distance of] even a cubit or more. Since this practice is available in all directions for these windows, the meaning here is that one may apply [plaster] oneself or have it applied in all directions—in an area the size of the width of the window shutter—for the purpose of treating the window openings.

parammukhāvā.meaning_2: out of (their) presence; behind (their) back; indirectly
parammukhāvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it appears as parammukhāvā = parammukhā + vā. Sahadhammika (five) = pācittiya (pāci.226).
parammukhāvā.example_1: Tasmā yo bhikkhu pañcasu sahadhammikesu aññatarassa ‘‘ mayhaṃ bhattapaccāsaṃ tuyhaṃ dammī ’’ ti vā ‘‘ vikappemī ’’ ti vā evaṃ sammukhā vā ‘‘ itthannāmassa dammī ’’ ti (pāci.226) vā ‘‘ vikappemī ’’ ti vā evaṃ parammukhāvā paṭhamanimantanaṃ avikappetvā pacchā nimantitakule laddhabhikkhato ekasitthampi ajjhoharati, pācittiyaṃ.
parammukhāvā.translation_1: Therefore, if a bhikkhu, having not performed a formal disposal regarding the first invitation—whether face-to-face [by saying] to one of five fellow practitioners, 'I give you my desire for rice' or 'I dispose of it,' or face-to-face [by saying] 'I give it to so-and-so' or 'I dispose of it,' or likewise when out of [their] presence—swallows even a single grain of boiled rice obtained from a family that has invited him later, he commits an offense of expiation.

navanītantiādimāha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Quotation joined to the following words: navanītaṃ iti ādim āha ('he said starting with "navanīta"'). The quotation mark is dropped. Could also be analysed as navanītaṃ + iti + ādi + āha.

apassayituṃ.meaning_2: to lean against; to rely on
apassayituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is paired with ālambituṃ: 'to lean against or to hold onto'. Apa + si (with the causative *e sign) gives apasseti.
apassayituṃ.example_1: Tassa tato laddhaṃ phalaṃ na vaṭṭati, durupaciṇṇadukkaṭañca āpajjati, aññassa taṃ vaṭṭati, phalirukkhaṃ pana apassayituṃ vā ālambituṃ vā vaṭṭati, paṭiggahetvā ṭhapite yaṃ aññaṃ aṅkurādi uppajjati, paṭiggahitameva taṃ.
apassayituṃ.translation_1: For him, the fruit obtained from that is not allowable, and he commits an offense of wrong conduct [for] wrongly practiced [action]; it is allowable for another; it is allowable to lean against or hold onto a fruit tree; whatever other sprout and so on arises [on an object] that has been placed after being accepted, that [sprout] is already accepted.

vettatintiṇikamātuluṅgakapiṭṭhakosambaka.meaning_2: drinks made from small fruits such as jujube, tamarind, citron, wood-apple, bel-fruit and elephant-apple, etc.
vettatintiṇikamātuluṅgakapiṭṭhakosambaka.construction: vettatintiṇika + mātuluṅga + kapiṭṭha + kosamba + karamanda + ādi + khuddaka + phala + pāna
vettatintiṇikamātuluṅgakapiṭṭhakosambaka.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A long bahubbīhi compound listed in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī among the eight drinks and their equivalents; nominative plural neuter in the text. The first member vettatintiṇika is uncertain (perhaps read vettatinduka, jujube).
vettatintiṇikamātuluṅgakapiṭṭhakosambaka.example_1: Ambapānaṃ jambupānaṃ cocapānaṃ mocapānaṃ madhukapānaṃ muddikapānaṃ sālūkapānaṃ phārusakapānanti imāni aṭṭha pānāni, yāni ca tesaṃ anulomāni vettatintiṇikamātuluṅgakapiṭṭhakosambakaramandādikhuddakaphalapānāni, etāni sabbāni anupasampannehi sītodakena madditvā katāni ādiccapākāni vā yāva rattiyā pacchimayāmaṃ nidahitvā paribhuñjitabbato yāmakālikāni nāma.
vettatintiṇikamātuluṅgakapiṭṭhakosambaka.translation_1: Mango-syrup, jambu-syrup, wild-plantain syrup, domestic-plantain syrup, honey-syrup, grape-syrup, water-lily syrup, and phārusaka-syrup—these eight drinks, and those that are their equivalents, such as small-fruit drinks [from] jujube, tamarind, citron, wood-apple, bel-fruit, and elephant-apple—all these are called “watch-of-the-night food” because they are to be consumed after having been stored until the last watch of the night, having been made by unordained persons [using] cold water or made by the heat of the sun.

padīpujjālanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The word occurs in the phrase padīpujjālanaṃ vā pattapacanādīsu jotikaraṇaṃ vā, an example of a reason for kindling a fire. Nominative singular neuter.
padīpujjālanaṃ.example_1: Samādaheyyāti jāleyya, aññatra tathārūpappaccayāti padīpujjālanaṃ vā pattapacanādīsu jotikaraṇaṃ vāti evarūpaṃ paccayaṃ vinā.
padīpujjālanaṃ.translation_1: 'Should light' (samādaheyya) means should kindle, and 'except for a suitable reason' (aññatra tathārūpappaccayā) means except for such suitable reasons as lighting a lamp, or making a fire for [the purpose of] drying an almsbowl and so on.

upasampajjitabbaṃ.meaning_2: to be ordained; should be ordained; fit to receive higher ordination
upasampajjitabbaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Potential participle expressing duty. In the text it is used impersonally with puna, 'one should again be ordained'. From upa + saṃ + √pad (go, step), the same root as upasampadā.
upasampajjitabbaṃ.example_1: Sopi yāva na jānāti, tāva tassa neva saggantarāyo na mokkhantarāyo, ñatvā pana puna upasampajjitabbaṃ.
upasampajjitabbaṃ.translation_1: And as long as he does not know it, there is for him neither an obstruction to heaven nor an obstruction to liberation; however, having known, he should be ordained again.

vicchindane.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text, meaning 'in the breaking (of the act)'. Could also be read as feminine vicchindanā; the PEU gives both.
vicchindane.example_1: Tattha āmisaparibhoge ekappayogena bahūpi dadato vā gaṇhato vā ekaṃ pācittiyaṃ, vicchindane sati payoge payoge pācittiyaṃ.
vicchindane.translation_1: There, in the sharing of requisites, there is one offence entailing confession for giving or receiving many things by a single effort; if there is a break [in the act], there is [an offence] for each effort.

ājānitabbaṃ.meaning_2: should be known; should be understood; is to be recognized
ājānitabbaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive potential participle of ājānāti (Skt bu-nā-ti type), used as a grammatical explanation of aññātabbaṃ; nominative singular neuter in the text.
ājānitabbaṃ.translation_1: 'Needs to recognize' (aññātabbaṃ) means: it should be known or understood.

vivaṇṇane.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text locative singular in vivaṇṇane, governed by vivaṇṇanavatthusmiṃ ("case of disparaging the Vinaya"); also in vivaṇṇane dukkaṭaṃ ("wrong doing for disparaging").
vivaṇṇane.example_1: Sāvatthiyaṃ chabbaggiye ārabbha vinayavivaṇṇanavatthusmiṃ paññattaṃ, sādhāraṇapaññatti, anāṇattikaṃ, tikapācittiyaṃ, anupasampannassa vivaṇṇane tikadukkaṭaṃ, ubhinnampi aññadhammavivaṇṇane dukkaṭameva.
vivaṇṇane.translation_1: It was laid down at Sāvatthī regarding the group of six bhikkhus concerning the matter of disparaging the Vinaya; it is a common laying down, not involving a command, an offense entailing confession, an offense of wrong conduct for a non-ordained person disparaging [it], and just an offense of wrong conduct for both [ordained and non-ordained] disparaging other [Dhamma] teachings.

aññadhammavivaṇṇane.meaning_2: disparaging another teaching; denigration of other doctrines
aññadhammavivaṇṇane.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text, in a Vinaya context; refers to disparaging teachings other than the Vinaya/Dhamma.
aññadhammavivaṇṇane.example_1: Sāvatthiyaṃ chabbaggiye ārabbha vinayavivaṇṇanavatthusmiṃ paññattaṃ, sādhāraṇapaññatti, anāṇattikaṃ, tikapācittiyaṃ, anupasampannassa vivaṇṇane tikadukkaṭaṃ, ubhinnampi aññadhammavivaṇṇane dukkaṭameva.
aññadhammavivaṇṇane.translation_1: It was laid down at Sāvatthī regarding the group of six bhikkhus concerning the matter of disparaging the Vinaya; it is a common laying down, not involving a command, an offense entailing confession, an offense of wrong conduct for a non-ordained person disparaging [it], and just an offense of wrong conduct for both [ordained and non-ordained] disparaging other [Dhamma] teachings.

garahitukāmatā.meaning_2: state of wanting to reproach; desire to blame; wish to disparage
garahitukāmatā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Abstract noun in -tā from garahitukāma (one who wants to reproach), itself garahituṃ + kāma. Nominative singular in the text, listed as one of two aṅgas.
garahitukāmatā.example_1: Garahitukāmatā ca, upasampannassa santike sikkhāpadavivaṇṇanañcāti imānettha dve aṅgāni.
garahitukāmatā.translation_1: The two factors here are: a desire to disparage, and disparaging the training rules in the presence of an ordained person.

sikkhāpadavivaṇṇanañcāti.meaning_2: disparaging the training rules, thus; 'disparagement of the training rules' (iti)
sikkhāpadavivaṇṇanañcāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sikkhāpadavivaṇṇanaṃ + iti, marking the end of a quoted phrase; nominative/accusative neuter in -aṃ before the quotative iti.
sikkhāpadavivaṇṇanañcāti.example_1: Garahitukāmatā ca, upasampannassa santike sikkhāpadavivaṇṇanañcāti imānettha dve aṅgāni.
sikkhāpadavivaṇṇanañcāti.translation_1: The two factors here are: a desire to disparage, and disparaging the training rules in the presence of an ordained person.

vivaḍḍhitaṃ.root_base: √vaḍḍh + a > vaḍḍha > vaḍḍhi (irreg); vi + √vaḍḍh + *e > vaḍḍhe (caus) > vaḍḍhi (irreg)
vivaḍḍhitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle of vivaḍḍhati (to increase, grow, expand). In the sentence it modifies vivādādhikaraṇaṃ: 'a legal question increased by disputes and quarrels'. Accusative singular neuter. The form could also be analysed as a causative past participle. The PEU entry suggests a reading vivaḍḍha, but the text has vivaḍḍhitaṃ. For the simple root √vaḍḍh the passive stem is vuḍḍha; the form vaḍḍhita is irregular.
vivaḍḍhitaṃ.translation_1: In the eighth, “who are arguing” means those who have arrived at a legal question that has been increased by disputes and quarrels.

avippavāsasammutisanthatasammutibhattudd.meaning_2: agreement (for) living apart from the three robes, (for) covering with grass, meal-announcer, dwelling-assigner, storekeeper, robe-receiver, porridge-distributor, fruit-distributor, solid-food distributor, distributor of minor things, rain-robe receiver, bowl-receiver, groundskeeper-overseer, and novice-overseer
avippavāsasammutisanthatasammutibhattudd.construction: avippavāsa + sammuti + santhata + sammuti + bhattuddesaka + senāsanaggāhāpaka + bhaṇḍāgārika + cīvarappaṭiggāhaka + yāgubhājaka + phalabhājaka + khajjabhājaka + appamattakavissajjaka + sāṭiyaggāhāpaka + pattaggāhāpaka + ārāmikapesaka + sāmaṇerapesaka + sammuti
avippavāsasammutisanthatasammutibhattudd.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A very long compound, functioning as a single term summarizing the thirteen saṅghakammas enumerated in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī. It appears in the nominative singular with -īti; the -iti is a quotation marker. The compound is analysed as a dvanda or as a list of agreements, with the final sammuti meaning 'agreement'. The individual members may be analysed differently; for example, bhattuddesaka is 'meal-announcer' and senāsanaggāhāpaka is 'dwelling-assigner'.
avippavāsasammutisanthatasammutibhattudd.example_1: Sīmāsammuti ticīvarena avippavāsasammutisanthatasammutibhattuddesakasenāsanaggāhāpakabhaṇḍāgārikacīvarappaṭiggāhakayāgubhājakaphalabhājakakhajjabhājakaappamattakavissajjakasāṭiyaggāhapakapattaggāhāpakaārāmikapesakasāmaṇerapesakasammutīti etāsaṃ sammutīnaṃ vasena sammuti veditabbā.
avippavāsasammutisanthatasammutibhattudd.translation_1: “Agreement” should be understood by way of these agreements: border-setting, [the agreement for] living apart from the three robes, [the agreement for] grass-covering, [for] the meal-announcer, [for] the dwelling-assigner, [for] the storekeeper, [for] the robe-receiver, [for] the porridge-distributor, [for] the fruit-distributor, [for] the solid-food distributor, [for] the distributor of minor things, [for] the rain-robe receiver, [for] the bowl-receiver, [for] the overseer of the groundskeeper, [and] the novice-overseer agreement.

saṃrakkhaṇatthaṃ.meaning_2: for the purpose of protecting; for the sake of guarding
saṃrakkhaṇatthaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Adverbial accusative of saṃrakkhaṇattha, a compound of saṃrakkhaṇa and attha meaning 'for the purpose of protecting'. Occurs in the phrase varasenāsanādīnaṃ saṃrakkhaṇatthaṃ.
saṃrakkhaṇatthaṃ.example_1: Thāvarena pana thāvaraṃ, itarena ca akappiyena mahagghakappiyena vā itaraṃ saṅghassa upakāraṃ sallakkhetvā kappiyaparivattanena parivattetuṃ vaṭṭati, varasenāsanādīnaṃ saṃrakkhaṇatthaṃ lāmakāni vissajjetuṃ vissajjetvā paribhuñjituñca vaṭṭati.
saṃrakkhaṇatthaṃ.translation_1: However, it is proper to exchange a valuable item for a valuable item, or for another unsuitable item or a valuable suitable item, by way of a proper exchange, after noting the benefit to the Saṅgha; it is [also] proper to discard inferior [dwellings] for the purpose of protecting high-quality dwellings and so on, and to use [the proceeds] after discarding them.

ayathālakaṃ.meaning_2: iron plate; iron dish; iron bowl
ayathālakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative/accusative singular in the text, in a list of vessels. Could be read ayathālakaṃ = aya + thālakaṃ or aya + thāla + ka.
ayathālakaṃ.example_1: Pāḷiyaṃ pana anāgatānipi bhiṅgārapaṭiggahauḷuṅkadabbikaṭacchupāti taṭṭakasarakasamuggaaṅgārakapalladhūmakaṭacchuādīni khuddakānipi garubhaṇḍāneva, ayapatto ayathālakaṃ tambalohathālakanti imāni pana bhājanīyāni, kaṃsalohavaṭṭalohabhājanavikati saṅghikaparibhogena vā gihivikaṭā vā vaṭṭati, puggalikaparibhogena na vaṭṭati.
ayathālakaṃ.translation_1: In the Pāli, even those not mentioned—such as water-pitchers, water-receivers, spittoons, hand-washing bowls, ladles, spoons, bowls, platters, cups, boxes, fire-trays, smoke-spoons, and so on—even if small, are still valuable items. However, iron bowls, iron platters, and copper-bronze platters are distributable items. It is proper to use [the latter] by way of Saṅgha-use or if they are modified by laypeople, but it is not proper to use them by way of personal-use.

ārakaṇṭakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A small pointed metal tool listed among allowable metal goods in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī; nominative/accusative singular in -aṃ. Sometimes masc in the PEU.
ārakaṇṭakaṃ.example_1: Ṭhapetvā pana taṃ bhājanavikatiṃ aññasmimpi kappiyalohabhaṇḍe añjanī añjanisalākā natthudānaṃ kaṇṇamalaharaṇī sūci khuddako pipphaliko khuddakaṃ ārakaṇṭakaṃ kuñcikā tāḷaṃ kattarayaṭṭhi vedhako bhindivālako yathātathāghanakatalohaṃvippakatalohabhaṇḍañca sabbaṃ bhājanīyaṃ.
ārakaṇṭakaṃ.translation_1: Apart from those copper-bronze vessels, in any other suitable metal goods, an ointment-stick, a nose-drop stick, a nose-drop tube, an ear-wax remover, a needle, a small knife, a small awl, an iron hook, a lock, a walking stick, a drill, a small dart, and any metal goods that are crafted in various ways are all distributable.

āmāsampi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text in the compound āmāsampi anāmāsampi, joined with -pi; adjective agreeing with senāsanaṃ. The PEU entry treats it as a noun meaning 'stroking'.
āmāsampi.example_1: Senāsanaparibhoge pana āmāsampi anāmāsampi sabbaṃ vaṭṭati.
āmāsampi.translation_1: In the use of dwelling-places, however, everything, whether touched or untouched, is proper.

lābukatumbaṃ.meaning_2: gourd-shell bottle; calabash flask; vessel made from a gourd
lābukatumbaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in a Vinaya list of small allowable vessels (bhājanīya); a vessel of gourd-shell, paired with lābukaghaṭa. Both parts may be read as neuter, so the gender is not certain.
lābukatumbaṃ.example_1: Mañcapīṭhānaṃ pādā ca aṭaniyo ca vāsiparasuādīnaṃ daṇḍā cāti etesu yaṃkiñci aniṭṭhitaṃ bhājanīyaṃ, tacchitamaṭṭhaṃ pana garubhaṇḍaṃ hoti, anuññātavāsiyā daṇḍo chattaṃ muṭṭhipaṇṇaṃ kattarayaṭṭhi upāhanā araṇisahitaṃ dhammakaraṇo pādaggaṇhanakato anatirittaṃ āmalakatumbaṃ āmalakaghaṭo lābukatumbaṃ lābukaghaṭo visāṇatumbanti sabbametaṃ bhājanīyaṃ, tato paraṃ garubhaṇḍaṃ.
lābukatumbaṃ.translation_1: The legs and rails of couches and benches, and the handles of adzes, axes, etc.—any of these that are unfinished are distributable; finished, smoothed ones are valuable items. The handle of an allowed adze, umbrella, palm-leaf fan, walking stick, sandals, fire-drill, water-strainer, or any small water-pitcher not exceeding the size of a bowl, small water-pot, small gourd, or small horn-flask are all distributable; anything beyond that is a valuable item.

lābukaghaṭo.meaning_2: gourd pot; water pot made from a gourd shell
lābukaghaṭo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Vinaya commentary listed among small bhājanīya vessels (lābukatumba, lābukaghaṭa, visāṇatumba). Nominative singular in the text.
lābukaghaṭo.example_1: Mañcapīṭhānaṃ pādā ca aṭaniyo ca vāsiparasuādīnaṃ daṇḍā cāti etesu yaṃkiñci aniṭṭhitaṃ bhājanīyaṃ, tacchitamaṭṭhaṃ pana garubhaṇḍaṃ hoti, anuññātavāsiyā daṇḍo chattaṃ muṭṭhipaṇṇaṃ kattarayaṭṭhi upāhanā araṇisahitaṃ dhammakaraṇo pādaggaṇhanakato anatirittaṃ āmalakatumbaṃ āmalakaghaṭo lābukatumbaṃ lābukaghaṭo visāṇatumbanti sabbametaṃ bhājanīyaṃ, tato paraṃ garubhaṇḍaṃ.
lābukaghaṭo.translation_1: The legs and rails of couches and benches, and the handles of adzes, axes, etc.—any of these that are unfinished are distributable; finished, smoothed ones are valuable items. The handle of an allowed adze, umbrella, palm-leaf fan, walking stick, sandals, fire-drill, water-strainer, or any small water-pitcher not exceeding the size of a bowl, small water-pot, small gourd, or small horn-flask are all distributable; anything beyond that is a valuable item.

thupikāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is thupikāti = thupikā + iti, at the end of a list of clay goods (tiles, bricks etc.). The PEU derives it from thūpa + ṇvu + ā in the sense 'pinnacle, many-tiered height'.
thupikāti.example_1: Mattikābhaṇḍe sabbaṃ manussānaṃ upabhogaparibhogaṃ ghaṭapiṭharādikulālabhājanaṃ, pattakaṭāhaṃ aṅgārakaṭāhaṃ dhūmadānakaṃ dīparukkhako dīpakapallikā cayaniṭṭhakā chadaniṭṭhakā thupikāti sabbaṃ garubhaṇḍaṃ, etesu pana vuttanayesu garubhaṇḍesu yaṃkiñci veḷuādiṃ attano atthāya gaṇhantena samakaṃ vā atirekaṃ vā phātikammaṃ katvā gahetabbaṃ.
thupikāti.translation_1: Among clay goods, all potter's goods belonging to people—potters' vessels such as jars and covers, bowl-trays, fire-trays, incense-burners, lamp-stands, lamp-trays, bricks, roofing-tiles, and spires—are valuable items; if one takes any of these bamboo goods and so on for one's own purpose, one should take them after performing an intensifying factor, equal or superior.

khīyitukāmatāya.meaning_2: desire to blame; wish to criticize; intention to reproach
khīyitukāmatāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Abstraction from khīyitukāma (desirous of blaming), itself from khīyituṃ (inf of khīyati, √khī, 'exhaust, destroy' used in the sense 'blame, reproach') + kāma + -tā. Instrumental singular in the text.
khīyitukāmatāya.example_1: Upasampannatā, dhammena laddhasammutitā, saṅghena saddhiṃ vikappanupagacīvaradānaṃ, pacchā khīyitukāmatāya khīyanāti imānettha cattāri aṅgāni.
khīyitukāmatāya.translation_1: The four factors here are: being ordained, having obtained sanction according to Dhamma, donating a robe capable of being formally shared together with the Saṅgha, and criticizing with the intention of criticizing later.

tiṃsakakaṇḍe.meaning_2: the section (of the Vinaya) containing thirty rules; the Nissaggiya Pācittiya section
tiṃsakakaṇḍe.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text. A traditional name for the Nissaggiya Pācittiya section of the Vinaya, which has thirty rules.
tiṃsakakaṇḍe.translation_1: In the twelfth [rule] of the Timsakakaṇḍa, the explanation of the training rule regarding the transfer of ownership follows the same method as previously stated.

āmāsaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Spelling with long ā in the first syllable (āmāsa) for āmasa. Nom. sg. āmāso; accusative singular in the text.
āmāsaṃ.example_1: Anuññātaṭṭhāne gahetvā nikkhipantassa, yaṃ hoti āmāsaṃ ratanasammataṃ, taṃ vissāsaṃ vā tāvakālikaṃ vā uggaṇhantassa, paṃsukūlasaññāya gaṇhato, ummattakādīnañca anāpatti.
āmāsaṃ.translation_1: There is no offense for one who picks it up and stores it away in a permitted place, for one who picks up what is perceived as a precious thing that is usable, for one who takes it on trust or temporarily, for one who takes it with the perception of it being discarded cloth, or for the insane and so on.

anivāsetvā.meaning_2: not having worn; not wearing; without putting on (the lower robe)
anivāsetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Negative absolutive used in Vinaya discussion of parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsanaṃ; in the text it takes an object understood from context (the lower robe). The na is joined to nivāsetvā; the positive form is nivāsetvā.
anivāsetvā.example_1: Idāni parimaṇḍalanti ettha nābhimaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchādetvā jāṇumaṇḍalassa heṭṭhā jaṅghaṭṭhikato paṭṭhāya aṭṭhaṅgulamattaṃ nivāsanaṃ otāretvā nivāsentena parimaṇḍalaṃ nivatthaṃ nāma hoti, evaṃ anivāsetvā anādariyena purato vā pacchato vā olambetvā nivāsentassa dukkaṭaṃ.
anivāsetvā.translation_1: Now, herein regarding parimaṇḍalan, one should understand the decision thus: it is called 'wearing evenly all around' for one who wears [it] after covering the circle of the navel and letting [it] down to the extent of eight fingerbreadths from the shinbone below the circle of the knees; for one who does not wear [it] thus, but out of disrespect wears [it] while letting [it] hang down in front or behind, there is an offense of wrong conduct.
anivāsetvā.example_2: Iti imaṃ khandhake paṭikkhittañca olambakañca sabbaṃ vivajjetvā vuttalakkhaṇasampannaṃ nibbikāraṃ parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsetabbaṃ, tathā anivāsetvā yaṃkiñci vikāraṃ karontassa dukkaṭaṃ.
anivāsetvā.translation_2: Thus, [one] should wear [the robe] 'evenly all around'—without distortion, endowed with the stated characteristics—after avoiding all this [wearing style] that is forbidden and hanging down in the Khandhaka; there is an offense of wrong conduct for one who does any distortion [by] not wearing [it] thus.

saṃvalliyaṃ.meaning_2: folded up; rolled up; (a robe worn) in folds
saṃvalliyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A listed manner of wearing robes in the Cūḷavagga; neuter accusative singular in the text, quoted from the Vinaya.
saṃvalliyaṃ.example_1: Na kevalañca tasseva, ye caññe ‘‘ tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā gihinivatthaṃ nivāsenti, hatthisoṇḍakaṃ macchavālakaṃ catukkaṇṇakaṃ tālavaṇṭakaṃ satavalikaṃ nivāsenti, saṃvalliyaṃ nivāsentī ’’ ti khandhake (cūḷava.280) nivāsanadosā vuttā, tathā nivāsentassapi dukkaṭameva.
saṃvalliyaṃ.translation_1: And not only for that [monk], but it is also an offense of wrong conduct for those others who wear [it] in the ways stated in the Khandhaka—where the faults of wearing [the robes] are mentioned, [saying]: 'At that time, the group of six monks wore [robes] as the laity wear [them], [they] wore [them] like an elephant's trunk, [like] a fish's tail, [with] four corners, [like] a fan, [with] a hundred folds, [or] folded up.'

coḷikaitthīnaṃ.meaning_2: woman of Coḷa; woman from the Coḷa country
coḷikaitthīnaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive plural in the text (coḷikaitthīnaṃ), compared to the elephant-trunk style of wearing a lower robe. Coḷikā is the name of a country in southern India.
coḷikaitthīnaṃ.example_1: Tattha hatthisoṇḍakaṃ nāma nābhimūlato hatthisoṇḍasaṇṭhānaṃ olambakaṃ katvā nivatthaṃ coḷikaitthīnaṃ nivāsanaṃ viya.
coḷikaitthīnaṃ.translation_1: Therein, hatthisoṇḍakaṃ is called wearing [a robe] by making [it] hang down from the navel-base in the shape of an elephant's trunk, like the wearing [of garments] by the women of the Coḷa [country].

obhujitvā.meaning_2: having folded up; having curled up; having wrapped
obhujitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of a verb obhujati, formed with prefix ava and √bhuj 2 (bend). In the text it describes folding up a long robe (dīghasāṭakaṃ obhujitvā).
obhujitvā.example_1: Satavalikaṃ nāma dīghasāṭakaṃ anekakkhattuṃ obhujitvā ovaṭṭikaṃ karontena nivatthaṃ, vāmadakkhiṇapassesu vā nirantaraṃ valiyo dassetvā nivatthaṃ.
obhujitvā.translation_1: Satavalikaṃ is called wearing [a robe] by folding up a long robe many times and making [it] into a roll, or wearing [it] after displaying continuous folds on the left and right sides.

saṃvalliyanti.meaning_2: is rolled up; is gathered together; is collected
saṃvalliyanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Not found in the sentences; third person plural passive-like form. Possibly from valliyati; see saṃvalliyati. Root √vall (turn).

paṭisaṅgharitvā.meaning_2: having folded; having tucked in; having arranged (a robe)
paṭisaṅgharitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it describes arranging the robe: having tucked the edges in and covered the neck down to the wrists. The i in -saṅgharitvā is a linking vowel before -tvā.
paṭisaṅgharitvā.example_1: Tatiye suppaṭicchannoti suṭṭhu paṭicchanno, gaṇṭhikaṃ paṭimuñcitvā anuvātantena gīvaṃ paṭicchādetvā ubho kaṇṇe samaṃ katvā paṭisaṅgharitvā yāva maṇibandhaṃ paṭicchādetvā antaraghare gamissāmīti attho, tathā akatvā pana jāṇuṃ vā uraṃ vā vivaritvā gacchantassa dukkaṭaṃ.
paṭisaṅgharitvā.translation_1: In the third, well-covered means well-covered. The meaning is: “Having fastened the button, having covered the neck with the trailing edge, having placed both edges evenly, having folded [them], and having covered [the body] down to the wrists, I will walk among the houses.” However, for one who does not do so, but walks having exposed the knees or the chest, there is a dukkaṭa offense.

hariṭakādīni.meaning_2: myrobalan and other (fruits); things beginning with myrobalan
hariṭakādīni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Neuter plural ending in -īni in the text, in a list of things placed in the mouth while teaching. The compound refers to myrobalan (Terminalia chebula) and similar fruits.
hariṭakādīni.example_1: Yo pana dhammaṃ kathento hariṭakādīni mukhe pakkhipitvā katheti, yattakena vacanaṃ aparipuṇṇaṃ na hoti, tattake mukhamhi sati vaṭṭati.
hariṭakādīni.translation_1: However, if one speaks while teaching the Dhamma with items like myrobalan in the mouth, provided the mouth contains only as much as does not make one's speech indistinct, it is proper.

tepaṇṇāsa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A cardinal number. In the text it qualifies sesāni (remaining sikkhāpadas).
tepaṇṇāsa.translation_1: The remaining fifty-three training rules vary by their origins such as the first Pārājika, and so on.

samanatthañceva.meaning_2: and the purpose of settling; and the purpose of calming
samanatthañceva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of samanatthaṃ (accusative of samanattha, 'purpose of settling', from samati) with ca eva; glosses samathāya in the text. Alternative analysis: samana + attha + ca + eva.
samanatthañceva.example_1: Samathāya vūpasamāyāti samanatthañceva vūpasamanatthañca sammukhāvinayo dātabbo … pe … tiṇavatthārakoti ime satta samathā dātabbā.
samanatthañceva.translation_1: ‘For settlement, for appeasement’ means that for the sake of both settling and appeasing, a verdict in the presence of [the parties] should be given... and the covering over as with grass, these seven settlements should be given.

upavadanā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Abstract noun from upavadati; in the text paired with codanā, 'reproach and accusation'.
upavadanā.example_1: Sīlavipattiyā vā ācāradiṭṭhiājīvavipattiyā vā anuvadantānaṃ yo anuvādo upavadanā ceva codanā ca, idaṃ anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ nāma.
upavadanā.translation_1: The censure—which is both reproof and accusation—that those who accuse [others] of a fall from virtue, conduct, views, or livelihood, is called litigation because of an accusation.

āmajjanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it explains āmasana (touching, rubbing) as pressing against something without moving away from the place touched. Nominative singular in -aṃ.
āmajjanaṃ.translation_1: 'Rubbing' (āmasanaṃ) means vigorous rubbing, and jostling (saṅghaṭṭanaṃ) in that same place without exceeding the area touched.

nevaattanāpaṭicodanā.meaning_2: not accusing oneself; not complaining about oneself; (a rule about) not accusing oneself nor informing the group
nevaattanāpaṭicodanā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound name of a rule in the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga (neva attanā paṭicodanā). Locative singular in the text; the sandhi na + eva is written neva.
nevaattanāpaṭicodanā.example_1: Sāvatthiyaṃ thullanandaṃ ārabbha nevaattanāpaṭicodanā nagaṇassa ārocanavatthusmiṃ paññattaṃ, sesamettha sappāṇakavaggamhi duṭṭhullāpattippaṭicchādanasikkhāpade vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.
nevaattanāpaṭicodanā.translation_1: It was laid down at Sāvatthī concerning Thullananda, in the matter of neither accusing her herself nor informing the group. The rest here should be understood according to the method stated in the Sapāṇaka-vagga regarding the training rule on concealing a serious offense.

ārociyamāne.meaning_2: being informed; being announced; being made known
ārociyamāne.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative absolute singular in the text; causative passive sense of āroceti.
ārociyamāne.example_1: Yathā vā tathā vā hi ārociyamāne paṭhamārocane bhikkhuniyā dukkaṭaṃ, dutiye thullaccayaṃ.
ārociyamāne.translation_1: For when information is provided in any way whatsoever, upon the first information the bhikkhunī incurs an offense of wrong conduct, and upon the second, an offense entailing suspension.

gumbavatiādīhi.meaning_2: such as gumbavatī and so on; beginning with gumbavatī
gumbavatiādīhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental plural in the text, in a list of concealment terms. The first member is probably a feminine noun in -ī (gumbavatī, perhaps 'thicket'), but the spelling gumbavati- is uncertain.
gumbavatiādīhi.example_1: Aññissā pana āgantukāya santike ārocetvā nikkhipitabbaṃ, nikkhittakālato paṭṭhāya pakatattaṭṭhāne tiṭṭhati, tato purearuṇeyeva catūhi bhikkhunīhi taṃ bhikkhuniṃ gahetvā gāmūpacārato ca bhikkhūnaṃ vihārūpacārato ca dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvā mahāmaggā okkamma gumbavatiādīhi paṭicchanne okāse nisīditabbaṃ.
gumbavatiādīhi.translation_1: However, it should be discarded after informing [a bhikkhunī] in the presence of another visiting bhikkhunī. From the time it is discarded, she stands in the normal state. Then, before dawn, four bhikkhunīs should take that bhikkhunī, pass beyond the two khandhas [of territory]—from the village vicinity and the bhikkhus' monastery vicinity—move away from the main road, and sit in a concealed place, such as in a thicket or fence.

bhājāpanaṃ.meaning_2: causing to be distributed; having (it) distributed; distribution
bhājāpanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative verbal noun; accusative singular in the text, object of adhiṭṭhāya in the phrase lesena bhājāpanaṃ.
bhājāpanaṃ.example_1: Akālacīvaratā, tathāsaññitā,‘‘ kālacīvaran ’’ ti adhiṭṭhāya lesena bhājāpanaṃ, paṭilābhoti imānettha cattāri aṅgāni.
bhājāpanaṃ.translation_1: The four factors here are: the state of being out-of-season cloth, the perception of it as such, having determined it as “in-season cloth” and having it distributed by a ruse, and the acquisition.

viññāpāpanaṃ.meaning_2: causing to make known; having (someone) inform; getting (another) to ask for; causing to intimate
viññāpāpanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Double causative of viññāpeti. In the text it is paired with viññāpana: asking for oneself versus getting another to ask; nominative singular in -aṃ.
viññāpāpanaṃ.example_1: Sattannaṃ dhaññānaṃ aññatarassa viññāpanaṃ vā viññāpāpanaṃ vā, paṭilābho, bhajjanādīni katvā vā kāretvā vā ajjhoharaṇanti imānettha tīṇi aṅgāni.
viññāpāpanaṃ.translation_1: The three factors here are: the intimation or having intimation [done] for one of the seven types of grain, the acquisition, and the roasting and so on followed by the swallowing.

chaḍḍāpanaṃ.meaning_2: causing to discard; having (it) thrown away; getting rid of
chaḍḍāpanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular in the text, paired with chaḍḍanaṃ; part of a list of five factors in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī.
chaḍḍāpanaṃ.example_1: Uccārādibhāvo, anolokanaṃ, valañjanaṭṭhānaṃ, tirokuṭṭatiropākāratā, chaḍḍanaṃ vā chaḍḍāpanaṃ vāti imānettha pañca aṅgāni.
chaḍḍāpanaṃ.translation_1: The five factors here are: the state of being excrement and so on, the non-looking, the place for disposal, the state of being outside a wall or fence, and the discarding or having [it] discarded.

chaḍḍāpentiyā.meaning_2: causes to discard; has (something) thrown away; makes (someone) abandon
chaḍḍāpentiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of chaḍḍeti. Present participle feminine genitive/locative singular chaḍḍāpentiyā in the text, parallel with chaḍḍentiyā.
chaḍḍāpentiyā.example_1: Tāni vatthūni chaḍḍentiyā vā chaḍḍāpentiyā vā purimanayeneva āpatti, tādise ṭhāne nisīditvā antamaso udakaṃ pivitvā matthakacchinnaṃ nāḷikerampi chaḍḍentiyā āpattiyeva.
chaḍḍāpentiyā.translation_1: There is an offense for one who discards those things or has them discarded, in accordance with the previous method; if she sits down in such a place and discards even water, or a coconut from which the top has been cut, it is an offense.

vadhantiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine form vadhantī, here instrumental singular vadhantiyā. Present participle in -anta from the root √vadh (hurt, slaughter), meaning striking or beating oneself.
vadhantiyā.example_1: Sāvatthiyaṃ caṇḍakāḷiṃ ārabbha attānaṃ vadhitvā rodanavatthusmiṃ paññattaṃ, kevalaṃ vadhantiyā vā rodantiyā vā dukkaṭameva.
vadhantiyā.translation_1: It was laid down in Sāvatthī concerning Caṇḍakāḷī regarding the occasion of weeping after striking herself; for one who only strikes or only weeps, it is merely an offense of wrong conduct.
vadhantiyā.example_2: Ñātirogabhogabyasanehi phuṭṭhāya kevalaṃ rodantiyā eva na vadhantiyā, ummattikādīnañca anāpatti.
vadhantiyā.translation_2: For one afflicted by misfortune regarding relatives, illness, or wealth, [there is no offense] if she only weeps and does not strike herself; nor is there an offense for the insane and so on.

visibbitadivasato.meaning_2: from the day of unsewing; counting from the day the robe was unsewn
visibbitadivasato.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Ablative singular in -to of the compound visibbitadivasa (vi + sibbita + divasa, 'day of unsewing'). The word is not in the given related entries, so the analysis is inferred. In the text visibbitadivasato pañca divase atikkāmetvā means 'after five days have passed from the day of unsewing'.
visibbitadivasato.example_1: Aññatra catūhapañcāhāti visibbitadivasato pañca divase atikkāmetvā ‘‘ neva sibbissāmi, na sibbāpanāya ussukkaṃ karissāmī ’’ ti dhuraṃ nikkhittamatte pācittiyaṃ.
visibbitadivasato.translation_1: 'Apart from four or five days' means that after five days have passed from the day of unsewing, when one has relinquished responsibility [by thinking], 'I will neither sew it myself nor make an effort to have it sewn,' there is an offense of expiation.

antarāyikinī.meaning_2: obstructed; having an obstacle; subject to impediment
antarāyikinī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine form of antarāyika, agreeing with the bhikkhunī implied in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī passage on sewing robes; nominative singular.
antarāyikinī.example_1: Yā pana antarāyikinī vā hoti, pariyesitvā vā kiñci na labhati, karontī vā pañcāhaṃ atikkāmeti, tassā ca, gilānāya ca, āpadāsu ca, ummattikādīnañca anāpatti.
antarāyikinī.translation_1: But for one who has an obstruction, or who does not obtain anything after inquiring, or who exceeds five days while doing [the sewing], or for one who is ill, in emergencies, or for the insane and so on, there is no offense.

visibbāpanaṃ.meaning_2: causing to be unstitched; having (a robe) unstitched; getting (a robe) unsewn
visibbāpanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative action noun from vi + √siv (sew), paired with visibbana in the Vinaya rule on robes. Nominative/accusative singular in the text.
visibbāpanaṃ.example_1: Nivāsanapārupanupagacīvaratā, upasampannāya santakatā, sibbanatthāya visibbanaṃ vā visibbāpanaṃ vā, aññatra anuññātakāraṇā pañcāhātikkamo, dhuranikkhepoti imānettha pañca aṅgāni.
visibbāpanaṃ.translation_1: The five factors here are: it being a robe intended for wearing or wrapping, it being the property of a fully ordained person, the act of unsewing or having it unsewn for the purpose of sewing, the exceeding of five days apart from an authorized reason, and the relinquishing of responsibility.

otāpanavasena.meaning_2: airing; drying (in the sun); exposing to heat
otāpanavasena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular in otāpanavasena, in the phrase paribhogavasena vā otāpanavasena vā, glossed in the commentary as airing robes in the sun. Alternative analysis as a masculine otāpana does not fit the neuter abstract sense here.
otāpanavasena.example_1: Saṅghāṭīnaṃ cāro saṅghāṭicāro , paribhogavasena vā otāpanavasena vā saṅghaṭitaṭṭhena ‘ saṅghāṭī ’ ti laddhanāmaṃ ticīvaraṃ, udakasāṭikā, saṃkaccikāti imesaṃ pañcannaṃ cīvarānaṃ parivattananti attho.
otāpanavasena.translation_1: A saṅghāṭicāro (outer robe period) is the wandering of [one's] saṅghāṭīs (outer robes). It refers to the rotation of these five kinds of robes that have acquired the name saṅghāṭī because they are held together for the sake of usage or for airing [in the sun]: the three robes, the bathing cloth, and the chest-wrapper.

paṭidātabbaṃ.meaning_2: to be given back; to be returned
paṭidātabbaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Potential participle used in the sense of obligation; neuter nominative singular in the text, agreeing with cīvaraṃ.
paṭidātabbaṃ.example_1: Pañcame cīvarasaṅkamanīyanti saṅkametabbaṃ cīvaraṃ, aññissā santakaṃ anāpucchā gahitaṃ puna paṭidātabbaṃ pañcannaṃ aññataraṃ cīvaranti attho.
paṭidātabbaṃ.translation_1: In the fifth [case], 'the robe that should be given back' means a robe that ought to be moved; specifically, it refers to any one of the five robes belonging to another [bhikkhunī] that was taken without asking and must be returned.

atāvakālikatāti.meaning_2: the state of not being temporary; fact of not being limited to a time
atāvakālikatāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Negative abstract noun (na + tāvakālika + -tā) forming the third of three factors (aṅga) for a samaṇacīvara; nominative singular in -tāti (atāvakālikatā + iti) at the end of the sentence.
atāvakālikatāti.example_1: Samaṇacīvaratā, ṭhapetvā sahadhammike ca mātāpitaro ca aññesaṃ dānaṃ, atāvakālikatāti imānettha tīṇi aṅgāni.
atāvakālikatāti.translation_1: The three factors here are: its status as a contemplative robe, giving it to others setting aside co-religionists and parents, and [the giving] not being temporary.
